bullets.title: Kimi K3 triggers semis selloff; consensus debate: bearish for capex or bullish for demand?
bullets.body: China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 (2.8T-parameter MoE model), igniting a DeepSeek-déjà-vu selloff—TMT Momentum down ~40% in 17 days (fastest/deepest on record vs. -29% in early 2021), SOX approaching bear market (-20%), NDX futures -1.75%, KOSPI -6.3%. However, MS and JPM both argue K3 is net bullish for compute: the model requires GB/B300 chips, cannot fit on a single DGX B200, and Chinese AI companies (Z.ai $1B+ ARR, DeepSeek $400-500M) are building real revenue. JPM separately notes K3's API pricing jumped 223% from predecessor and cost-per-task is higher than Grok/Claude, limiting US adoption.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure names off 24-40% from highs on multiple compression, not earnings deterioration
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks (MS, Mizuho, UBS, JPM) stress that the AI hardware pullback is driven by positioning unwind and multiple compression—not fundamental deterioration. Hyperscaler consensus expects 2027 AI CapEx just over $1.1T; MS sizes the market at $1.4T with 4x compute capacity by 2028. Prime brokerage flows show memory stocks account for ~2/3 of tech selling since the reversal, with global memory down -36% and US AI Tech Beneficiaries down -24%.

bullets.title: Momentum factor crash at 96th historical percentile; algorithmic reversals risk cascade
bullets.body: Widely-held momentum trades are breaking immediate-term support levels, triggering algorithmic selling. The momentum factor's volatility sits at the 96th historical percentile, and Hedgeye notes machine-trading switches flip when support breaks. Separately, high-beta stocks are down >20% and tracking for their worst month since the 2008 GFC, while 74% of stocks were up +2.4% yesterday—the selling is concentrated in crowded tech/semi names, not broad market.

bullets.title: Fed: July pause near-certain; September hike odds at 33-50%; core PCE expected ~0.19% m/m
bullets.body: Markets are pricing a 96% probability of no change at the July 29 FOMC and 33% probability of a 25bp hike in September (CME Fedwatch shows 74% odds of higher rates in 2026). Morgan Stanley forecasts June core PCE at 0.19% m/m (3-month annualized 3.08%), representing the first clean inflation reading in six months. Dallas Fed's Logan took a hawkish stance urging modestly higher rates; Fed Vice Chair Jefferson signaled willingness to reconsider stance if inflation does not moderate.

bullets.title: Iran-Gulf conflict escalating: Kuwait power plant hit, Hormuz traffic at 3-week low, oil ~$80
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC claimed attacks on the U.S. Al Udeid base in Qatar and struck Kuwait's water desalination and power plant; CENTCOM is on its sixth day of heavy airstrikes on Iranian military targets near Bandar Abbas. Strait of Hormuz crossings dropped to a 3-week low with only 8 confirmed on July 16, 7 of which were Iranian-route. Despite the escalation, Brent remains ~$80/barrel—analysts note Trump's continued military freedom is contingent on oil staying below ~$100.

bullets.title: US-China tech tensions rising: Kimi K3 framed as geopolitical flashpoint, not just AI event
bullets.body: Trump accused China of illegally accessing US voter data, and Xi Jinping positioned China's open-weight AI models as a global public good at WAIC. Analysts warn the US-China tech truce (in place since late 2025) looks increasingly fragile, with risk of US executive actions restricting Chinese open-weight models or further semiconductor restrictions. Beijing's likely retaliation channel is critical mineral export delays/tightening. Xi's planned Washington visit (tentatively late September) is at increased political risk.

bullets.title: Housing starts +19% m/m in June but driven by multifamily; single-family flat, permits fell 3%
bullets.body: June housing starts came in at 1,427k (+19% m/m vs. consensus +11.2%), entirely driven by a multifamily rebound—single-family starts were unchanged at 895k. Building permits declined 3.0% m/m to 1,367k. Morgan Stanley and PSC Macro both characterize overall housing as moving sideways for 2+ years, with no breakout expected.

bullets.title: Industrial production +0.1% m/m in June; manufacturing at cycle high, breadth softening
bullets.body: US industrial production rose 0.1% m/m in June, below the 0.2% consensus, but manufacturing output sits at a cycle high. Ex-auto and tech manufacturing was down for two consecutive months; semiconductor IP decelerated to 0.5% m/m. Capex and manufacturing are broadening economic activity beyond pure AI/tech, with 54.6% of industries posting monthly gains.

bullets.title: Early Q2 earnings broadly strong: card spending accelerating, consumer resilient, loans broadening
bullets.body: Card spending accelerated sharply across major banks—JPM +10%, BAC +9%, Citi +12%, WFC +9%, Amex +16% YoY—with delinquency trends better than expected across all FICO scores. Loan demand is broadening beyond AI into industrial, equipment leasing, and working capital. The K-shaped economy narrative is losing support as both lower and higher income cohorts show strength, though WFC flags large capital deployment and potential leverage risks.

bullets.title: META hiring AWS Compute chief signals potential enterprise cloud business launch
bullets.body: Meta is hiring Dave Brown, one of AWS's most senior executives with nearly two decades at Amazon, to lead cloud infrastructure. MS views this as a signal of an aggressive enterprise cloud/infrastructure push, consistent with Meta's $125-145B 2026 capex guidance and its Louisiana data center expansion from 2GW to 5GW ($50B+ commitment).

bullets.title: Open-source AI adoption accelerating; UBS says this is bullish for NVDA inference demand
bullets.body: UBS estimates open-source token utilization grew from sub-1% last year to multiple times that by mid-2026, with most open-source models trained/fine-tuned on NVDA hardware, yielding superior inference performance. The shift toward cost optimization and consumption-based pricing is driving model selection focus, but UBS argues open-source adoption expands total inference demand rather than cannibalizing it. MSFT is transitioning Copilot from seat-based to consumption pricing.

bullets.title: GOOGL Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed ~1 month; stock -4.5% on capability gap vs. peers
bullets.body: GOOGL dropped 4.5% after announcing Gemini 3.5 Pro would be delayed approximately one month due to coding capability gaps versus competitors. The delay adds to broader AI model competition concerns and is cited by Citi and UBS as a near-term negative catalyst alongside NFLX's miss.

bullets.title: NFLX -11%: 3Q guidance disappoints, UCAN slowing, multiple compression fears resurface
bullets.body: Netflix fell 11% as 3Q revenue growth decelerates to +11% ex-FX vs. +12% in 2Q, with UCAN slowing on pricing timing. Bears are now pointing to potential compression toward traditional video media multiples. Morgan Stanley cut PT to $83 from $90; Bernstein cut to $95 from $100. NFLX is trading at a 52-week low, down 45.6% YTD.

bullets.title: VIX +10% to 18.45; SPX 7,480 cited as critical support; OPEX-driven gamma cliff next week
bullets.body: VIX jumped 10.3% to 18.45 intraday. OPCO flags SPX 7,480 as a knife-edge pivot—a break below risks market-wide leveraged selling next week post-OPEX as positive gamma support diminishes. The weekly webinar notes VIX at 15 triggered vol ownership threshold and that August VIX calls are attractive. SPY put spreads seen as more efficient than QQQ protection given high tech weighting.

bullets.title: Japan -4% (Nikkei drawdown -11.4%), Shanghai -3.1%; hedge funds still too long both
bullets.body: Asian equity markets hit hard overnight: Nikkei fell 4.0% bringing its drawdown to -11.4% from the cycle peak; Shanghai declined 3.1% and remains in a bearish trend. Hedgeye notes hedge funds are still carrying elevated long positions in both Japan and NASDAQ-100, representing continued unwind risk.

bullets.title: Apple surpasses Nvidia as world's most valuable company at $4.92T; AAPL +57% YTD
bullets.body: Apple overtook Nvidia in market cap—AAPL at $4.92T vs. NVDA at $4.86T—as the semi selloff hit Nvidia while Apple is perceived as a relative safe haven (anti-AI capex play with raised prices, stable unit volumes, positive iPhone cycle momentum). AAPL is up 57.2% YTD trading at $330.40.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler debt capacity substantial; IG market not overwhelmed by AI issuance wave
bullets.body: JPMorgan's credit team argues concentration concerns around hyperscaler IG issuance are overstated—major hyperscalers could issue ~$1.7T additional debt before approaching a theoretical 3% index weight. YTD TMT IG supply rose to $329B; hyperscaler spreads widened meaningfully but the broader market remained relatively insulated. Investors likely to require greater spread compensation as AI funding needs expand.

bullets.title: BOJ signals no urgency for consecutive hikes; likely to raise growth forecast
bullets.body: BOJ officials see limited need for back-to-back rate increases, pointing to a measured approach to policy normalization. The BOJ is also expected to raise its 2024 growth forecast. The dovish signal comes as the Nikkei is already down 11.4% from cycle peak, adding pressure on yen-sensitive positioning.

bullets.title: Retail leverage at extremes; Korea 1-in-30 adults margin-called; leveraged ETF listings suspended
bullets.body: Leverage is elevated across markets. Korea saw retail exhaustion with 1 in 30 adults receiving margin calls; regulators are suspending leveraged ETF listings. In the US, leveraged ETF AUM metrics suggest SOXL unwinding may be only halfway complete. Multiple strategists flag the systemic fragility from leverage amplifying any further downside.

bullets.title: Week ahead: GOOGL/TSLA earnings Wed, INTC Thu, AMD AI event; Fed blackout before Jul 29 FOMC
bullets.body: Q2 earnings ramp significantly next week—GOOGL and TSLA report Wednesday after close, INTC Thursday after close. AMD hosts its Advancing AI event Wednesday-Thursday. The Fed is in blackout period ahead of the July 29 FOMC. Leading Indicators print Monday; jobless claims Thursday; Manufacturing/Services PMI and New Home Sales Friday.
